🐾 Here’s the story behind Matt’s payments work at **JP Morgan Chase**.

From **August 2009** to **June 2012**, Matt served as Technology Delivery Lead for ACCESS Next Generation, the bank’s global corporate banking portal. Its treasury operations ran on disparate regional systems, and Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform did not provide all the payment modules, security controls, or workflows the bank required. Each payment type had distinct formatting, validation, compliance, and settlement requirements, with aggressive delivery timelines.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and the US. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, working through where the platform’s native capabilities ended and bespoke engineering was required.

He designed and delivered ACH credits and direct debits, wire payments, FX/cross-border payments, and federal tax payment capabilities. That included NACHA file validation, integration with the bank’s foreign exchange engine, and Message Authentication Code security so corporate users could verify payment integrity before release. He also delivered the centralized payments gateway, handling message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**, rather than retaining fragmented point-to-point integrations.

The surrounding controls were part of the work: payment-type-specific permissions, sanctions screening, transaction-monitoring integration, and contextual guidance within payment screens. His user administration engine replaced individual permission configuration with role-based profiles and bulk changes, reducing entitlement management from days to minutes.

Matt also led payments data migration without disruption to live payment operations. For regional rollout, he translated local regulatory requirements into data visibility and access controls, sequencing launches by regulatory readiness rather than a single global deployment.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, consolidating regional systems into a unified portal serving **135,000+** clients across **180+ countries**. Matt’s production responsibilities included on-call incident response, root-cause analysis, and leadership updates while payment issues were live.

🐾 Here’s what Matt has built, changed, and delivered.

Matt’s work spans Execution & Delivery, Org & Working-Model Transformation, and Talent & Enablement: building product engineering organizations, changing how teams work, and shipping production software.

At **Accenture**, clients wanted to move away from waterfall delivery, siloed teams, and feature factories. Matt built the Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from the ground up, with full P&L accountability. He recruited and developed **150+ practitioners** across engineering, architecture, product, and design. He brought those disciplines together in balanced teams, with pair programming, test-driven development, customer research, and thin-slice, production-ready delivery.

He also built the training behind those practices. New hires often lacked hands-on cloud-native or Agile experience. Matt paired junior hires with experienced mentors, established skills matrices and career pathways, and used an “I do, we do, you do” learning model. The centers achieved near-zero attrition in their first **2 years**.

At **Capital One**, slow iterations and misaligned priorities were extending time-to-market. Matt assembled a balanced team of **8**, working from a client-prioritized, testable backlog. Engineers followed red-green-refactor: write a failing test, write minimal code to pass it, then safely refactor. The team delivered features **3 to 4 times faster** than other **Accenture** teams on the same engagement, with **zero production defects**. The client sought to retain the team beyond the planned end.

At **Norfolk Southern**, rising defects contradicted near-complete test coverage. Matt took ownership in front of the client and account leadership rather than defending the dashboard. He audited the code and tests, exposed vague backlog stories, brought in TDD experts, and rebuilt the work through hands-on coaching. The client stopped finding defects the dashboard could not see.

Across the centers, teams delivered **30+ product engagements** for **15+ Fortune 500 clients**, with **4X faster velocity** and **zero-defect deployments**. Delivery excellence, repeat engagements, and client referrals contributed to **\$100M+ in repeatable business**.

The team delivered features **3 to 4 times faster** than other **Accenture** teams on the same engagement, with **zero production defects**. The client sought to retain the team beyond its planned end. At **Norfolk Southern**, mission-critical operations tools went live with **zero production defects**.

Across the centers, Matt delivered **30+ product engagements** across **15+ Fortune 500 clients** and contributed to **\$100M+ in repeat business** through delivery excellence and client relationships.
